card.name: Is/are after drug combination subject
card.fires_on: The verb "is" or "are" right after a subject naming a drug combination or at-risk group, just before a restriction or risk statement. Seen in interaction and warning sections.

modes.label: Drug combination subject
modes.description: "is" follows a concomitant use or coadministration subject, before "not recommended" or "contraindicated".
modes.example: Coadministration of fluconazole and quinidine<< is>> contraindicated. (See CONTR

modes.label: At-risk group subject
modes.description: "are" follows a vulnerable group such as premature neonates, before "particularly at risk".
modes.example: Premature neonates<< are>> particularly at risk because their kidneys are immature

card.writes: The promoted tokens (moment) and suppressed tokens (only, best) do not suggest a clear output effect on the next word.
card.plain: It marks the verb "is" or "are" that comes just before a statement that a drug combination is not recommended or a group is at risk.
